newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian cocaine king said appealing jail term.
newsitem.headline: Colombian cocaine king said appealing jail term.

text.p: Colombia's billionaire cocaine king Miguel Rodriguez Orejuela is appealing his 23-year jail term for drug-trafficking, saying it is "unjust," local media reported on Sunday.

The former No.2 of the mighty Cali cartel, which at one time was estimated by U.S. countrnarcotics agents to supply 80 percent of the world's cocaine, was sentenced to 23 years behind bars last weekend.

He was initially sentenced to a nine-year stretch, which would in practice have seen him walk free in less than five years, but that was upped after an anonymous, or so-called "faceless," judge convicted him of another drug smuggling charge that he had not previously admitted.

The NTC TV news programme said Rodriguez Orejuela wrote to the prosecutor's office saying he would contest the sentence and claimed it had been handed down under pressure from the United States. A spokesman for the prosecutor's office was not available for comment.

U.S. officials complained the drug kingpin's punishment was ridiculously light and were angry that a new law to impose tougher penalties for drug-related offences -- including a maximum 60-year jail term -- could not be applied retroactively to Rodriguez's crimes.

The United States "decertified" Colombia for a second consecutive year, in a decision announced on Friday, for its failure to crack down hard enough on drug-trafficking. It has repeatedly said that Rodriguez and his brother Gilberto, the former cartel chieftain, continue to run their criminal empire from behind bars.
NTC also reported an investigation had been launched after the judge who increased Rodriguez's sentence began to receive death threats.
